questions.questionText: What does brute-force vector search actually do?
options: It randomly samples a few chunks and returns them
It compares the query embedding against every stored chunk embedding, then returns the top-k most similar
It only compares against the single most recently added chunk
It retrains the embedding model for each query
questions.correctAnswer: It compares the query embedding against every stored chunk embedding, then returns the top-k most similar
questions.explanation: Brute-force search is exactly the direct application of cosine similarity from the embeddings lesson, applied against every stored vector, then sorted and truncated to the top-k.

questions.questionText: Why does brute-force search stop being practical at very large scale (millions of vectors)?
options: It doesn't, brute force scales infinitely with no cost
It's O(n) in the number of stored vectors, so comparing against every single one becomes too slow as the collection grows very large
Brute-force search only works with fewer than 10 vectors
It requires retraining the embeddings for each new query
questions.correctAnswer: It's O(n) in the number of stored vectors, so comparing against every single one becomes too slow as the collection grows very large
questions.explanation: At thousands of vectors, O(n) brute force is fast enough; at millions, comparing against every single one becomes a real bottleneck, motivating ANN index structures like HNSW.

questions.questionText: Why might a RAG pipeline apply a minimum similarity threshold, rejecting a query if even the best match scores too low?
options: A low best-match score signals the knowledge base likely doesn't contain a good answer, which should be surfaced explicitly rather than handing the model a barely-relevant chunk
Thresholds are only used to save storage space
It has no real purpose, it's just a convention
questions.correctAnswer: A low best-match score signals the knowledge base likely doesn't contain a good answer, which should be surfaced explicitly rather than handing the model a barely-relevant chunk
questions.explanation: Without a threshold, a query with no good match in the knowledge base still gets handed whatever chunks scored highest (even if weakly relevant), which can mislead the generation step into using irrelevant context.
